priorStories.headline: Haiti sends 18 assassination suspects to US
priorStories.body:
Eighteen suspects in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse were flown from Haiti to the United States to face trial, according to U.S. and Haitian officials.

U.S. prosecutors have indicted 30 people in the case. Haiti’s justice minister said proceedings there had produced no trial after five years of delays.

priorStories.headline: Ukraine launches vast drone attack across Russia
priorStories.body:
Ukrainian forces launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, according to officials cited by the Associated Press. Russian authorities reported three deaths in the Moscow region and damage to an oil refinery and residential buildings.

Ukraine said it targeted oil and logistics facilities. The casualty, interception and damage reports come from the countries fighting the war and could not be independently reconciled.

candidates.summary: Russia's Central Election Commission said United Russia won 57.83% of the party-list vote after more than 95% of ballots were counted in the parliamentary election. The preliminary result would give the ruling party 355 of the State Duma's 450 seats, preserving its constitutional majority. The election was conducted under tight political controls, with voting also held in Russian-controlled areas of Ukraine that Kyiv and Western governments reject as illegally occupied.
candidates.title: United Russia retains constitutional majority in preliminary count

candidates.summary: China's Foreign Ministry announced that President Xi Jinping will make a state visit to the United States from September 23 through September 25 at President Donald Trump's invitation. The ministry did not provide further itinerary details in its initial announcement.
candidates.title: China confirms Xi state visit to United States

candidates.summary: Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain and strong winds to eastern Japan as it approached the Pacific coast. At least 275 flights were canceled, more than 4,000 households in Chiba Prefecture lost power, some railway services were suspended and authorities warned of flooding and landslides. Japan's weather agency said rainfall through Tuesday could exceed the monthly September average in some areas.
candidates.title: Typhoon Dujuan disrupts travel and power in eastern Japan

candidates.summary: The Gates Foundation announced that it is convening a coalition of 60 organizations, including Anthropic, Google and the OpenAI Foundation, to develop more representative language data for artificial intelligence. The coalition aims to make AI tools more accessible to more than 3 billion people over five years, though details including its governance remain under development.
candidates.title: Gates Foundation convenes coalition for underrepresented AI languages

candidates.summary: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee said persistent supply shocks, including oil-price increases and tariffs, may require higher interest rates that push employment below its target to return inflation to 2%. His remarks described a policy trade-off and did not announce a Federal Reserve decision.
candidates.title: Goolsbee says inflation fight may require economic pain

candidates.summary: U.N. Special Rapporteur Mariana Katzarova presented a report to the Human Rights Council describing Russian surveillance, intimidation and reprisals against critics abroad as a systematic state strategy. The report, based on about 400 documented cases, said recorded incidents increased after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia's Geneva mission did not immediately respond to Reuters and Moscow has previously denied allegations of hostile actions abroad.
candidates.title: UN expert reports expanded Russian repression abroad

sources.name: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights

candidates.summary: An unidentified projectile struck a tanker entering the Strait of Hormuz, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center. Two crew members sustained minor injuries, while the vessel continued toward its next port under its own power. No environmental impact was reported initially.
candidates.title: Projectile strikes tanker entering Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that renewed fighting in Yemen had displaced 129,438 people across seven provinces. The agency said 11,352 people were displaced during the three days beginning September 18, with many families having already fled their homes more than once.
candidates.title: Yemen fighting displaces nearly 130,000 people, IOM says

candidates.summary: Twelve states and the Writers Guild of America agreed to settle lawsuits challenging Paramount's $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Paramount committed to measures including increased U.S. film production, worker-support funding and monitoring of editorial independence. The settlements remove major legal obstacles, but the states' agreement still requires a judge's approval.
candidates.title: Paramount settles state and writers' challenges to Warner merger

candidates.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed seven bills imposing new disclosure and oversight requirements on data centers. The measures address electricity and grid-upgrade costs, water use, land use, workforce needs and local review, including provisions intended to prevent infrastructure costs from being shifted to other electricity customers.
candidates.title: California enacts data-center oversight package

candidates.summary: Texas Governor Greg Abbott directed the state environmental agency to halt permits sought by data centers until grid and water regulators complete audits of the facilities. The directive pauses state regulatory approvals but does not itself permanently prohibit data-center development.
candidates.title: Texas halts data-center permits pending audits

candidates.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration said it began using a predictive-analytics system intended to improve flight management and reduce congestion. Initial deployment covers airspace around Washington, D.C., with gradual expansion planned elsewhere under a 12-year contract awarded to Air Space Intelligence in June.
candidates.title: FAA begins deploying predictive flight-management system

candidates.summary: Pennsylvania's Department of Health reported 792 measles cases, 25 more than its September 18 count, and 155 hospitalizations. Lancaster County remained the state's hardest-hit area. Reuters reported that the state outbreak was part of the largest U.S. measles resurgence in decades.
candidates.title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak reaches 792 cases

candidates.summary: A Vermont jury convicted Jason Eaton on three counts of attempted second-degree murder for shooting three Palestinian American students in Burlington in November 2023. The verdict rejected his insanity defense. Sentencing will occur later; prosecutors said each count carries a presumptive minimum term of 20 years and a possible sentence of life without parole.
candidates.title: Vermont jury convicts gunman who shot Palestinian American students

candidates.summary: Moldova's government said it would ask parliament on September 22 to declare an energy and water-supply emergency because of dangerously low levels in the Dniester River and concerns about peak electricity capacity. The Security Council recommended emergency regulations, but parliament had not yet approved the requested declaration.
candidates.title: Moldova seeks emergency powers over water and energy risks

candidates.summary: Polo strengthened into a hurricane off Mexico's Pacific coast, with maximum sustained winds of 80 mph, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center. Its core was forecast to remain offshore, but forecasters warned of heavy rain, flooding, mudslides and hazardous seas in Guerrero and Michoacán. Further strengthening was forecast but had not yet occurred.
candidates.title: Polo becomes hurricane off Mexico's Pacific coast

candidates.summary: A business association representing community development financial institutions sued the U.S. Treasury Department, seeking to stop nearly $300 million in congressionally appropriated grants from expiring at the end of September. The group alleged Treasury unlawfully failed to distribute fiscal 2025 funding. Treasury did not immediately comment to Reuters.
candidates.title: Community lenders sue Treasury over withheld grants

candidates.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of emergency to mobilize resources and streamline preparations for expected El Niño-related winter storms. The proclamation was a preparedness measure rather than a report that the forecast severe winter impacts had already occurred. Newsom also terminated 34 older emergency declarations that were no longer needed.
candidates.title: California declares emergency for El Niño preparedness

candidates.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that renewed fighting in Yemen had displaced 129,438 people across seven provinces, including 11,352 during the three days beginning September 18. The World Food Programme's acting chief said the agency had provided meals or food commodities to about 60,000 people and was building supplies to assist hundreds of thousands more. The U.N. reported nearly 700 deaths in the escalation.
candidates.title: UN agencies expand response as Yemen displacement grows
